standards."},{"slide":4,"severity":"error","kind":"fact","problem":"The claim that IEEE 830 structures SRS documents and that both IEEE 830 and ISO/IEC 25010 reference use-case modeling is misleading because IEEE 830 was withdrawn in 2017 and neither standard defines use-case modeling.","fix":"State that IEEE 830 was a legacy SRS structure superseded by ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148, that ISO/IEC 25010 defines product-quality characteristics, and that UML use-case modeling is defined separately by OMG."},{"slide":4,"severity":"error","kind":"fact","problem":"The assertion that these standards are widely adopted in industry is unsupported and obscures that IEEE 830 is obsolete and ISO/IEC 25010 is a quality model rather than a requirements or use-case specification standard.","fix":"Replace the adoption claim with the standards' actual roles and current status, including the 2017 withdrawal of IEEE 830 and the 2018 edition of ISO/IEC 25010."},{"slide":4,"severity":"warning","kind":"fact","problem":"The reference to recent spec-driven development literature is vague and unverifiable, so students cannot judge which guidance is authoritative.","fix":"Name and cite the specific current standard or publication being referenced, or remove the claim."},{"slide":6,"severity":"error","kind":"fact","problem":"The notes incorrectly treat Payment and Inventory as use cases invoked by Place Order without showing the required include relationships or identifying the external Payment service as an actor.","fix":"Show Payment Service with converting a sufficiently detailed specification into implementation artifacts, but require human review and do not reliably consume arbitrary diagrams."},{"slide":8,"severity":"warning","kind":"clarity","problem":"The instruction to list every external role is too broad for the short product description and may cause students to invent actors that the description does not support.","fix":"Ask students to identify only actors evidenced by the description and to state assumptions for any additional roles."},{"slide":8,"severity":"warning","kind":"clarity","problem":"The example does not show how the derived use cases map to the actors, so it does not fully model the actor–use-case relationships
